source_text:
Τῷ μὲν οὖν ὀνόματι τῆς ὁδοῦ τὴν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον δηλοῖ περιβολὴν, ὅπερ ἔστι τῶν σωματικῶν καὶ τῶν ὁρατῶν· γῆς γάρ τι μόριον ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ
αἰσθητὸν ἔδαφος καθέστηκε· τὸ δὲ ὄνομα τῆς ἀληθείας <καὶ> τῆς ζωῆς τὴν τοῦ Πατρὸς φύσιν· ἡ γὰρ ἀλήθεια πρᾶγμά τι νοητὸν οὔτε ὄμμασιν οὔτε ἁφῇ ὑποπίπτον.
thought_title: The names way, truth, and life signify two natures
orientation: Eustathius is explaining the meaning of Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life' from John 14:6, distinguishing what each name signifies.
pass_a_gloss: By the name of the way, then, he indicates the covering according to man, which is of the bodily and visible things; for the way is a portion of earth and has been established as a perceptible ground. But the name of the truth and of the life indicates the nature of the Father; for truth is an intelligible thing falling under neither eyes nor touch.

choices.english: he indicates the covering according to man
choices.why: Keeps the adverbial force of κατὰ ἄνθρωπον as 'according to man' rather than turning it into an adjective, preserving the literal sense that the covering is human in kind.

choices.term: ὅπερ ἔστι τῶν σωματικῶν καὶ τῶν ὁρατῶν
choices.english: which is of the bodily and visible things
choices.why: Renders the genitive plural substantives literally as 'of the bodily and visible things,' keeping the partitive sense that the covering belongs to that class.
rejected: which consists of bodily and visible things

choices.term: γῆς γάρ τι μόριον ἡ ὁδὸς
choices.english: for the way is a portion of earth
choices.why: Preserves the predicate order and the indefinite τι as 'a portion,' matching the source's explanatory γάρ clause.
rejected: for the way is some part of the earth
for a way is a piece of ground

choices.english: has been established as a perceptible ground
choices.why: Renders καθέστηκε as 'has been established as' to keep the perfect's resultative force and the predicate complement structure.

choices.term: τὸ δὲ ὄνομα τῆς ἀληθείας <καὶ> τῆς ζωῆς τὴν τοῦ Πατρὸς φύσιν
choices.english: But the name of the truth and of the life indicates the nature of the Father
choices.why: Supplies the elided verb 'indicates' from the previous clause, as the Greek does, and keeps the article repetition 'of the truth and of the life' for the paired names.
rejected: but the name of truth and life signifies the Father's nature
but the names truth and life mean the Father's nature

choices.term: πρᾶγμά τι νοητὸν οὔτε ὄμμασιν οὔτε ἁφῇ ὑποπίπτον
choices.english: an intelligible thing falling under neither eyes nor touch
choices.why: Keeps πρᾶγμά τι as 'a thing' with the indefinite article, and renders ὑποπίπτον as 'falling under' to preserve the spatial metaphor of not coming under the senses.
rejected: an intelligible reality not subject to sight or touch
something intelligible that neither eyes nor touch perceive

bible_refs.note: The whole passage interprets Christ's saying 'I am the way and the truth and the life'; the source text here refers to 'the name of the way' and 'the name of the truth and of the life.'

pass_b_english: By the name “way,” then, he indicates the covering that belongs to his manhood—the covering that is one of the bodily and visible things. For a way is a portion of earth and stands as a perceptible ground. But the name “truth” and “life” indicates the nature of the Father, since truth is an intelligible thing that falls under neither eyes nor touch.
notes: The angle-bracketed <καὶ> before τῆς ζωῆς is an editorial supplement where the manuscript appears to lack the conjunction; the sense requires it.
